question: How should a menu row and a button be capitalised: Apply to Every Cut (the Mac) or Apply to every cut (the mocks)?
context: The mocks write menu rows in sentence case; the app writes all 127 of its menu rows in Mac title case. Four audits in three days explained the same difference. One rule settles it for good.

options.label: The Mac way: Title Case
options.summary: Every menu row, menu heading and button reads like the Mac menu bar: Apply to Every Cut, Reset to Defaults, Copy Look. Panel labels keep sentence case. The mocks stay as drawn and audits stop flagging the difference.
pros: Matches the rows macOS writes into our menus itself (Select All, Enter Full Screen, Hide Others), so no menu mixes two styles
Matches Photoshop, Premiere and Final Cut (Merge Down, Ripple Delete, Add Cross Dissolve)
127 of the app menu rows already read this way, so nothing a person sees changes
cons: Departs from every mock page, which writes rows in sentence case
options.mitigation: The rule names the departure once, so no audit has to explain it again, and the mocks keep their wording for everything else.

options.label: The mock way: Sentence case
options.summary: Every menu row, heading and button the app writes itself reads like the mocks: Apply to every cut, Reset to defaults, Copy properties. Rows macOS supplies stay in title case because the app cannot change them.
pros: The app matches the mocks word for word
Reads a little softer and more like prose
cons: The Edit and Window menus mix both styles, since macOS writes Select All and Enter Full Screen itself
Looks unlike every other Mac app and every pro tool
options.mitigation: Rewrite them in one pass behind a test, so the change lands at once instead of drifting row by row.

options.label: Menus the Mac way, buttons the mock way
options.summary: Menu rows and menu headings, in the menu bar and every right-click or panel menu, are Title Case. Buttons inside the panel (Draw a Curve, Use This Curve) keep the mock sentence case, like the labels beside them.
pros: Menus match macOS and the pro tools
Panel buttons read like the panel labels around them, as the mocks draw them
cons: Two rules to remember instead of one
A button and the menu row that does the same thing can be written differently
options.mitigation: The rule lists both cases side by side with examples, and the test checks each surface against its own style.
